text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- President Guntis Ulmanis lit the Christmas tree near the presidential palace.
- Parliament passed amendments to the law income tax, imposing a unified 25 percent rate on all income.

- President of Russian oil concern LUKoil, Vagid Alekperov, said his company is planning to invest 10-15 million lats in building a lubricants plant some 20 km south of Riga. He met Prime Minister Andris Shkele, Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans to discuss cooperation between LUKoil and the oil transit firm Ventspils Nafta.
- President Ulmanis announced that in 1997 he would seek to achieve more openness in the privatisation process and to involve the public in the fight against corruption.
- Parliament passed a bill on forming a free port in Ventspils, which is to become Latvia's second port after Riga.

- Creating more and more obstacles to the Baltic states on their way towards Europe has become a priority for Russian foreign policy instead of defending the interests of the Russian-speaking population.

- President Ulmanis believes that some provisions in the law regulating the privatisation of land in rural areas should be re-considered. One provision bans the purchase of land by non-citizens but allows it by foreign companies.

- Foreign Minister Valdis Birkavs believes that signing a visa-free deal with Denmark will provide the basis for talks on abolishing visa regulations between Latvia and the other Nordic nations. Talks with Norway are likely to start in February next year.
- The Bank of Latvia issued a licence to a new bank, Vereinsbank Riga, which is a branch of the German Vereinsbank und Westbank AG. The bank's authorised capital is 3.9 million lats.
- Baltcom GSM, Latvia's second GSM mobile phone operator, has completed construction of its network and will today make its first symbolic call to Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans.
